overall: The Board violated the Open Meeting Law by deliberating outside a posted meeting while drafting, circulating, polling on and releasing a racism statement; its June 30 vote did not cure this. Only immediate and future compliance was ordered.

allegations.summary: Board member's June 22 email to the full Board urged issuing a statement against racism as soon as possible, allegedly deliberating outside a posted meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, Ms. Miles’ June 22 email to the entire Board suggesting that it issue a statement on racism and expressing her belief that it should do so as soon as possible constituted deliberation outside of a posted meeting, in violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Emails among members and the chair about drafting, revising, approving and releasing the racism statement allegedly deliberated outside a posted meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Likewise, the emails concerning drafting, finalizing, approving, and releasing the statement also constituted deliberation outside of a posted meeting.

allegations.summary: Forwarding of the draft statement, carrying members' views, to other Board members allegedly constituted deliberation outside a posted meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Additionally, when Mr. Cyr, Ms. Miles, and the Town Administrator each forwarded the statement, which necessarily included the thoughts and opinions of the members who drafted it, to other members of the Board, this also constituted deliberation outside of a posted meeting.

allegations.summary: Contacting members outside a meeting to ask whether they would endorse the statement allegedly constituted polling in violation of the Open Meeting Law.
allegations.key_passage: Finally, the process of polling Board members outside of a properly posted meeting, as was done here when members were contacted regarding whether they would endorse the statement, constitutes a violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Board argued its June 30 meeting, where it discussed and voted to accept the statement, cured any earlier violation.
allegations.key_passage: Here, where the Board did not engage in independent, deliberative action, but rather simply voted to accept the statement as written, we find that the Board’s actions did not cure the prior deficiencies, and we find that the Board violated the Open Meeting Law.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law (no further remedial action ordered because the emails were already placed on file with the Town Clerk and made public).
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution that future similar violations may be considered evidence of an intent to violate the law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
